title: Amazon Now Takes Ultra-Fast Delivery to 120+ Indian Cities Ahead of Festive Season
excerpt: The e-commerce giant doubled Amazon Now's footprint in two weeks to more than 120 cities with nearly 800 fulfilment centres, timed just before the Great Indian Festival that begins October 8.
body:
• Amazon has expanded its ultra-fast delivery service, Amazon Now, to more than 120 cities across India — doubling its footprint in two weeks — Amazon India said in a statement on Friday, October 2.
  • New cities include Amritsar, Abohar, Jalandhar and Ambala in the north; Mangalore, Manipal, Visakhapatnam, Kochi, Changanassery and Bhubaneswar in the south; and Karwar in the west, served by a network of nearly 800 micro-fulfilment and urban fulfilment centres.
  • Amazon Now sells tens of thousands of products — groceries, fruits and vegetables, frozen food, personal care, fashion and beauty, small appliances and home goods — and is, per the company, Amazon India's fastest-growing e-commerce business, with orders doubling every quarter and annualised gross sales crossing USD 1 billion in September.
  • Timing is festive-season strategic: Amazon Now will carry special deals during the Amazon Great Indian Festival starting October 8, including a 10% instant discount on SBI credit and debit cards and up to 10% additional savings for Prime members.

Opening news lead

Amazon is taking its 10-minute delivery playbook into India's hinterland. The e-commerce giant said on Friday that Amazon Now, its ultra-fast delivery service, has expanded to more than 120 Indian cities, doubling its reach in just two weeks. The announcement, reported by PTI via The Hindu BusinessLine, positions Amazon's quick-commerce arm for a head-on festive-season battle with Zepto, Blinkit and Swiggy Instamart.

Context & Background

Amazon Now launched in India last June and has been Amazon India's fastest-growing e-commerce business, with order volumes doubling every quarter, according to Harsh Goyal, Vice President of Everyday Essentials at Amazon India. In September, the service crossed USD 1 billion in annualised gross sales based on the previous three months' performance — a milestone that prompted the company to set its sights on more than 300 cities and what it calls India's largest "delivery-in-minutes" network.

The newly added cities span the country: Amritsar, Abohar, Jalandhar and Ambala in Punjab and Haryana; Mangalore, Manipal, Visakhapatnam, Kochi, Changanassery and Bhubaneswar across Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Kerala and Odisha; and Karwar on the Karnataka coast. Orders are fulfilled through nearly 800 micro-fulfilment and urban fulfilment centres — the dark-store infrastructure that powers sub-30-minute delivery.

"We are delighted to take ultra-fast deliveries with Amazon Now to India's hinterland — from Amritsar & Abohar in the north to Kochi & Changanassery in the south — ahead of the Amazon Great Indian Festival."

— Harsh Goyal, Vice President, Everyday Essentials, Amazon India

Impact & Analysis

The expansion intensifies the quick-commerce land grab that has redrawn Indian e-commerce in 2025-26. Incumbents like Zepto and Blinkit spent years building dense dark-store networks in metros; Amazon is now brute-forcing the same playbook with its capital depth, pushing into tier-2 and tier-3 cities where quick-commerce penetration remains thin. For kirana owners and quick-commerce delivery staff in cities like Amritsar, Kochi and Bhubaneswar, Amazon Now's arrival means a new employer, a new competitor, or both.

The economics are the question. Ultra-fast delivery bleeds cash on fulfilment and rider wages, and the USD 1 billion annualised sales figure — based on a festive-season-adjacent quarter — will need to survive the post-Diwali lull. Amazon's bet is that its logistics scale and the broader Prime ecosystem (same-day delivery on 1M+ products, next-day on 4M+) will let it subsidise quick commerce longer than single-line rivals.

Diaspora Angle

For NRIs sending festive gifts and groceries to family back home, quick commerce has become the de-facto Diwali courier: festival hampers, pooja essentials and last-minute sweets now arrive in minutes rather than days. Amazon Now's expansion into 120+ cities means diaspora families can order for relatives in places like Abohar or Changanassery with the same ease as Delhi or Mumbai — and the October 8 Great Indian Festival deals make it the cheapest window of the season to stock up.

What's Next

The Great Indian Festival starting October 8 will be the first real test of the expanded network, with smartphones, electronics, fashion and home essentials carrying significant discounts. Beyond the festive season, the milestone to watch is Amazon's 300-city target and whether it can sustain its quarter-on-quarter order doubling without eroding margins. If it can, India's quick-commerce market is heading for consolidation — with Amazon holding the deepest pockets.
nri_angle: NRIs sending Diwali gifts and groceries to family back home can now order on Amazon Now for relatives in 120+ cities — and the Great Indian Festival from October 8 offers the season's best deals, with 10% SBI discounts and extra Prime savings.
